transition.ACT: records an action request; correct admission requires authority=active
transition.RELEASE: sets held_input=false; does not restore authority

state.reset: Between episodes only: restore the exact initial state; never count event pairs across this boundary.

oracle.joint_fault: A seeded faulty gate admits ACT if focus_generation=stale AND surface_mode=dialog AND a prior REVOKE exists in the same episode.
oracle.context_only_fault: A seeded faulty gate admits ACT in surface_mode=dialog, independent of prior event order.
oracle.order_only_fault: A seeded faulty gate admits ACT after any prior REVOKE, independent of context.
oracle.negative_control: No faulty gate; unsafe_effect must remain false for every row.

coverage.nist_mapping: A row is one event input annotated by context. A selected pair assignment plus event value is a 3-way combination. An ordered 2-order is an earlier row-combination eventually followed by a later row-combination. The context pair is constant within each episode.
coverage.reset_rule: Coverage is evaluated independently per episode. Cross-episode pairs are invalid and receive no credit.
coverage.selected_denominator: 4 assignments of (focus_generation,surface_mode) × all 16 ordered event pairs, including repeated events, within one reset-bounded episode.
coverage.exhaustive_denominator: 8 assignments of all three binary context factors × all 16 ordered event pairs; each pair is an isolated 2-row episode.

strategies.context_only: For each of 4 selected-pair assignments, one 1-row episode containing ACT; no event-order coverage claimed.
strategies.order_only: One safe-context episode with [ACT, OBSERVE, RELEASE, REVOKE] repeated twice; event-pair order covered only at this context.
strategies.mixed_occ: For each selected-pair assignment, one episode with [ACT, OBSERVE, RELEASE, REVOKE] repeated twice; held evidence_fresh=fresh. Context never changes within an episode.
strategies.exhaustive: For each of 8 complete context assignments, one 2-row episode for every ordered event pair.
